mutations.because: Dropping atrim leaves apad's silence padding unbounded (nothing tells it when to stop), so the muxer waits forever for the audio stream to reach EOF and the encode times out — verified by hand (encodeTimeoutMs: 5000) to reject with 'ffmpeg encode timed out after 5000ms' after ~5s; under the real 120s default this shows up as the whole audio.test.ts run taking ~90s longer, not as a clean assertion failure, but it still exits non-zero.

Dropping apad leaves a bed shorter than durationSec unpadded (atrim only cuts, never pads), so the audio stream's own decoded length stays at the bed's short natural length instead of durationSec. The container-level Duration line (this lane's earlier, wrong measurement) could not have caught this — the video track is still the full durationSec long and dominates it — only measuring the audio stream itself (probeAudioStreamDurationSec) does.

Always adding the second input (even without `audio`) breaks VE-D3: a brief that uses none of the new inputs must produce exactly today's argv, and the pinned no-audio args test fails once an extra -i appears.

Dropping -ar/-ac stops forcing a fixed sample rate and channel count, so the encoded stream's shape depends on the bed's own format and on this ffmpeg build's defaults instead of being pinned — the recorded golden could drift on a machine whose ffmpeg defaults differently. The with-audio args test did not previously assert either flag's presence, so this mutation would have gone uncaught before the assertion was strengthened.
